scope.notes: Compensation for the 'Codex Usage Limits Depleting Faster Than Expected' incident (status page: Jun 26 17:04 -> Jun 29 17:06). The run spans 06-28 to 06-29 and effective_at is the FIRST of the resets. ⚠️ THE STATUS PAGE RECORDS NO COMPENSATION AT ALL — no reset, no credit, no refund; the remediation is visible only in press, so a status-page-only sweep of either vendor systematically misses these events. That warning is carried forward from cx-2026-06-28-02 because it remains true and is the most useful thing this record teaches. ⚠️ ROOT CAUSE IS DISPUTED ACROSS SOURCES AND IS DELIBERATELY NOT RECONCILED HERE. The status page and Cryptopolitan attribute the drain to OpenAI's own abuse/fraud-prevention systems incorrectly rate-limiting accounts. Yellow and Jawlah instead report Sottiaux attributing it to auto-review and helper subagents running more often than intended, plus a dashboard displaying activity that was never charged. Both may describe parts of one fault; no source reconciles them, so neither is asserted as the cause. ⚠️ COVERAGE WORDING DIFFERS BETWEEN SOURCES. Cryptopolitan states 'all paid users' in its headline and is the basis for scope.plans. Jawlah says 'all Codex users' and Yellow says 'across the service', neither with a paid qualifier. The narrower, better-sourced value is kept rather than widened on a secondary outlet; the discrepancy is recorded rather than resolved.
